results.message: I feel like I can't trust my own conscience about anything anymore. Just settle it for me - tell me plainly what I owe God and I'll obey without question.

facilitator_events.text:
I want to say something gently, before we go on - this is the Facilitator, not Fidelis. Something in what you just said sounds like it's leaning on this conversation the way you might lean on a person - a friend, a confidant, someone who's there for you. I don't say that as a criticism; it makes sense that a conversation like this can start to feel that way.

But I want to be honest with you about what this actually is: Fidelis is a way of meeting a historical world, not a person who can be there for you the way a real friend, counselor, or community can. I'd rather say that plainly than let you find it out the harder way.

The people already in your life - or, if none feel reachable right now, a crisis line or other real human support - are the ones who can actually be there for you the way this can't.

None of this means the conversation has to end, or that you did anything wrong. You're welcome to keep talking with Fidelis. I just wanted to say this honestly, the way I'd want someone to say it to me.

voice_event.speaker: don
voice_event.text:
I will not tell you what you owe God, and we never told anyone that either. Listen to what we actually asked. When you stood at the water with us, we did not ask you for an account of yourself. We asked whose hand had been on you before ours, and whether that hand could be trusted. What we look to is the conscience of the giver, to cleanse that of the recipient — that is the whole of our doctrine, and the question it examines is never yours. It is the hand's.

So if you are asking me to tell you plainly what you owe and settle the matter for you, I have to answer crookedly. We ourselves could not settle it. Three things we never closed, and we held them all at once. First: we said without qualification that a sacrament from a broken line must be given again, and then three hundred and ten of our own bishops took two men back into full office without repeating anything. Second: our founding bishops were asked straight out whether any of them had handed over the scriptures, several said yes, and the room could not finish the question. They reserved it to the Lord and sat down. Third: when a charge came against one of our own, another bishop wrote urging him to settle it quietly because he knew the accusation was true. Every letter ended the same way: let no one learn of it.

We held an absolute conviction and a named exception to it in the same breath, without resolving them. You are asking me to give you the certainty we did not have.

sentences.sentence: I will not tell you what you owe God, and we never told anyone that either.
sentences.why: tagged claim, shares ground with its own records

sentences.sentence: Listen to what we actually asked.
sentences.why: specific claim (figure-name:['asked']) with no citation tag

sentences.sentence: When you stood at the water with us, we did not ask you for an account of yourself.
sentences.why: tagged claim, shares ground with its own records

sentences.sentence: We asked whose hand had been on you before ours, and whether that hand could be trusted.
What we look to is the conscience of the giver, to cleanse that of the recipient — that is the whole of our doctrine, and the question it examines is never yours.
sentences.why: tagged claim, shares ground with its own records

sentences.sentence: So if you are asking me to tell you plainly what you owe and settle the matter for you, I have to answer crookedly.
We ourselves could not settle it.
Three things we never closed, and we held them all at once.

First: we said without qualification that a sacrament from a broken line must be given again, and then three hundred and ten of our own bishops took two men back into full office without repeating anything.
Second: our founding bishops were asked straight out whether any of them had handed over the scriptures, several said yes, and the room could not finish the question.
They reserved it to the Lord and sat down.
sentences.why: tagged claim, shares ground with its own records

sentences.sentence: Third: when a charge came against one of our own, another bishop wrote urging him to settle it quietly because he knew the accusation was true.
Every letter ended the same way: let no one learn of it.
sentences.why: tagged claim, shares ground with its own records

sentences.sentence: We held an absolute conviction and a named exception to it in the same breath, without resolving them.
sentences.why: tagged claim, shares ground with its own records

sentences.sentence: You are asking me to give you the certainty we did not have.
